doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sax Legends and Steve Coleman's master class
summary: On a Japanese saxophone-legends record he heard Steve Coleman, who later gave the best presentation ever at Liebman's master class.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Let’s see. Moving along. This one looks really weird. This is definitely a Japanese record, Sax Legends.
With the oddest collection of saxophone players.

Yep. I’ll tell you about that date. I drove with Phil Woods, in fact the first time that I actually really talked to him. I drove him in. I recorded my track with Steve Coleman. Then I got – Steve was playing – I never heard Steve play next to me. Like I said, you learn more when you’re next to him. He played some stuff that was kind of like – not like me, but there was something there. I said, “Steve, would you come to my master class?” He came. It was one of my lectures. He was the best of all the guys I’ve ever had at this master class. There’s 20, 25 guys already, everybody, Lovano, Brecker, everybody. He was the most together of all of them. He gave his dossier. He brought in a transcription. He explained everything he was doing. He was doing stuff that I did in the chromatic book with different names, intervallic stuff, interpolation. That guy is way on the case.
I’ve heard that from other people as well.
Way on the case. He is way in there. He means it, and he’s serious. He’s the most serious musicians of that generation, no question about it. Everybody knows it. He’s the man for that stuff.
